belongs_to: Sum of Consecutive Numbers: 'Anshu is exploring sums of consecutive numbers. He has written the following -'

belongs_to: Math Talk: 'Take any 4 consecutive numbers. For example, 3, 4, 5, and 6. Place + and - signs in between the numbers. How many different possibilities exist? Write all of them.'
description: One small rectangular box with a pink border and white fill holding two lines of text: '3 + 4 – 5 + 6' and '3 – 4 – 5 – 6'. These are the first two of the eight possible sign patterns for 3, 4, 5, 6 (the other six are not shown).

belongs_to: Sum of Consecutive Numbers: 'Eight such expressions are possible. You can use the diagram below to systematically list all the possibilities.'
description: Left-to-right binary tree of sign choices for the numbers 3, 4, 5, 6. Black straight line segments, black text; every edge carries a small sign label ('+' above the upper edge of each pair, '–' below the lower edge). Level 0: one node '3' at the far left, vertically centred. Level 1: two nodes '4' (one upper, one lower); edge 3->upper 4 labelled '+', edge 3->lower 4 labelled '–'. Level 2: four nodes '5' (top to bottom: 5a, 5b, 5c, 5d); upper 4 -> 5a labelled '+', upper 4 -> 5b labelled '–'; lower 4 -> 5c labelled '+', lower 4 -> 5d labelled '–'. Level 3: eight nodes '6' in a column at the right, two per '5' (upper edge '+', lower edge '–'), so the leaves top to bottom correspond to sign patterns +++, ++–, +–+, +––, –++, –+–, ––+, ––– (counts: 1, 2, 4, 8 nodes; 2+4+8 = 14 edges). Only the top two leaves are completed: from the first '6' a black dashed line with an arrowhead points right to the red text '3 + 4 + 5 + 6', and from the second '6' a dashed arrow points to the red text '3 + 4 + 5 – 6'. The other six leaves have no arrow and no expression.
unclear: Edge-label positions are small; read from a zoomed crop, all 14 edges carry '+' (upper) or '–' (lower) as listed.

belongs_to: Math Talk: 'Now, take four other consecutive numbers ... Repeat this for one more set of 4 consecutive numbers. Share your findings.'
description: Three rectangular boxes side by side, each with an orange dashed border and white fill, each holding two lines then a column of three dots. Box 1 (filled): '3 + 4 – 5 + 6 = 8' and '3 – 4 – 5 – 6 = – 12', then three vertical dots. Box 2 (filled): '5 + 6 – 7 + 8 = 12' and '5 – 6 – 7 – 8 = – 16', then three vertical dots. The three vertical dots mean the remaining six expressions are not written.

belongs_to: Explanation 3: 'This can also be explained using the positive and negative token model ... The number of ways to choose 4 numbers a, b, c, d and combine them using + and - signs is infinite.'
